subject: Staged notification & forensic evidence staging — proposed DPA redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finserv.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Dino Rossi <dino.rossi@thirdparty-consult.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification windows and evidence handoff

Vivek,

Thanks again for the call earlier. To move our DPA review forward we need confirmation on two things: a) how Redwood intends to notify us and affected regulators/customers in the first 72 hours vs. the longer 21-day evidence staging window, and b) how subprocessors will be handled if they hold encrypted snapshots (we're particularly concerned about cross-border transfer and redaction).

A couple of asks from our side:
- Oral notification within 6 hours for high-severity incidents, followed by written notice within 72 hours that includes a scoped timeline and initial indicator of compromise (IOC) summary.
- A staged evidence handoff: a forensics snapshot (low-level telemetry + timestamps, tokenized session ids) under an escrow-like access arrangement, with PII redaction options before transfer.
- Clarify whether Redwood will require law enforcement subpoenas to unseal any encrypted fields maintained by subprocessors.

We attached our proposed redline (see DPA_redline_v2.pdf) and a short forensic checklist — would appreciate Redwood's comments by Monday so our legal + privacy teams can finalize.

Regards,
Sarah Tan
Head of Vendor Risk
FinServe Capital

Attachment stubs: DPA_redline_v2.pdf (PDF, 112KB); Forensic_Staging_Checklist.xlsx (Excel, 34KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finserv.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification windows and evidence handoff

Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and the redline. High level response below; I'll loop in Legal for precise contract language but wanted to get operational alignment first.

1) Notification cadence: we can support oral escalation (phone + secure channel) within 6 hours for incidents flagged as "Severity 1" by our incident triage, followed by a written notice with initial facts within 72 hours. We propose a two-tier written cadence: initial fact summary (72h) + investigative update at 7 days + evidence staging readiness notice at 21 days if further forensic transfer is required.

2) Evidence staging & redaction: Redwood maintains isolated forensic snapshots ( encrypted at rest ) and can produce tokenized telemetry plus timeline slices. For PII-sensitive exports, we support pre-transfer redaction and an agreed staging checklist (attached: Forensic_Staging_Checklist.xlsx). If a customer requests full raw snapshots, we require a documented justification and additional approval (legal + privacy) and an encrypted transfer method to an escrowed S3 bucket with time-limited keys.

3) Subprocessors & law enforcement: Redwood's standard position is to comply with lawful process. If a subprocessor holds encrypted material we control, we will coordinate access; if the subprocessor independently holds keys, Redwood will require them to follow the same cooperative process and notify us immediately. We can add a subprocessor cooperation clause that commits Redwood to use reasonable efforts to obtain access or to provide derivative (redacted/tokenized) evidence where keys are unavailable.

I attached an internal draft of the proposed flow (REDWOOD_INCIDENT_FLOW.png) that shows where oral vs. written notifications hit the timeline and recommended points for legal sign-off.

Next steps: Kimberly and Ben, can you review the technical feasibility of the 6h oral + 72h written promise and confirm any associated SLOs or constraints? I'll ask Legal to draft contract text that preserves our ability to sequence evidence exports while committing to good-faith cooperation. Sarah — if you can flag any non-negotiables in the redline that break the above, we'll prioritize those.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: REDWOOD_INCIDENT_FLOW.png (PNG, 48KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 13:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification windows and evidence handoff

Quick operational note — we can commit to the 6h oral for confirmed Severity 1 incidents where the triage system marks it as a "production-impacting data exposure" (this is consistent with our internal incident taxonomy). Caveats:
- The 72h written notice will include initial scope but may not include full root cause until the 7-21 day investigative window completes. We should ensure the contract language allows progressive disclosure.
- Forensic snapshots: we can produce tokenized traces (session ids, hashes, timestamps, bucket/object refs) within 7 days; full raw exports requiring decryption may take longer depending on subprocessor cooperation and key retrieval (if keys are held externally). We estimate 14-21 days for full, decrypted handoffs in cross-border scenarios.

Operational asks for Legal redline: include an explicit 'staged disclosure' section and define "tokenized evidence" vs "raw snapshot". Also add a clause allowing Redwood to redact customer identifying fields on a good-faith basis if required for legal/regulatory compliance before transfer.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Dino Rossi <dino.rossi@thirdparty-consult.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@finserv.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 15:48:00 +0200
Subject: RE: DPA — incident notification windows and evidence handoff

Vivek / Sarah / Kim — appreciate the proposed cadence. A couple of pragmatic points from my side as incident counsel for FinServe: 

- FinServe will accept staged disclosure if the DPA includes: (a) a guaranteed initial notice within 72 hours with an SLA for updates, (b) a mitigation summary in the 7-day update, and (c) firm commitments to either produce redacted tokenized evidence or, if keys are available, full decrypted snapshots within 21 days or an explanatory timeline if longer.
- Add an explicit cooperation obligation for subprocessors: they must respond to Redwood's coordination requests within 72 hours and provide an estimate for any key recovery operations. If a subprocessor refuses, Redwood must escalate to FinServe and provide the available derivative evidence.
- Suggest adding an optional fast-path: if FinServe provides a signed warrant/subpoena, Redwood agrees to accelerate unsealing efforts and provide additional support (subject to relocation/restrictions under local law).

If Redwood can accept the above, we can mark the DPA redline as provisionally acceptable and move to legal wording. I can draft suggested boilerplate language for the subprocessor cooperation clause if helpful.

Thanks,
Dino Rossi
Incident Counsel (external advisor)
ThirdParty Consulting
